title: Are We Still Good for Tomorrow?
scenario: A Product Manager and Full-stack Engineer discuss a newly discovered testing risk one day before a planned release and decide whether to reduce scope or move the release.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Hey, Daniel. Are we still good for tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: For most of it, yeah. But there's an issue with the recovery part.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: At stand-up this morning you said we were still on track. What did you find?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: I ran through the full flow this afternoon. Recovery touches a few more cases than I expected.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: More development work?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: A little, but that's not the main problem. I can probably finish the code. I'm more concerned about testing it properly before tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: How much more testing are we talking about?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Hard to say exactly. That's part of the problem. I found a couple of paths I hadn't accounted for, and I don't want to assume they're the only ones.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Okay. So if we keep everything in scope, what are you recommending?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Honestly, we'd have to move the release. I wouldn't be comfortable shipping the whole thing tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Moving everything is going to be difficult. Sales are already preparing around this release.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Yeah, I know.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Is recovery blocking the rest of the onboarding changes?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: No. That's the good news. We can separate them.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: So we could release the main flow tomorrow and leave recovery as it is?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Exactly. Then I can finish the recovery changes and test them properly for the next release.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Would users notice anything strange?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Not really. The current recovery flow would stay in place. The new onboarding changes would still work.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Okay. Why didn't this come up earlier?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: I didn't see it until I tested the full path today. The individual pieces looked fine. It was only when I put the whole flow together that the extra cases showed up.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Right.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: I should've flagged the uncertainty earlier, though. I was assuming the recovery piece was more isolated than it actually is.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Fair enough. If we take recovery out, are you confident about the rest?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Yes. The main flow is already in good shape. I'd still want tomorrow morning for final checks, but I'm comfortable with that.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: And if we don't take it out?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Then we're either rushing the testing or moving the release. I'd rather take that piece out than rush it.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Yeah, agreed.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Let's lock the scope there, then. Main onboarding changes tomorrow. Recovery moves to the next release.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Works for me.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Can you update the ticket and send me a quick note on what's moving?

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Yep. I'll do that now.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Thanks. And if anything else comes up in the final checks, flag it early.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Will do.

question.text: What do Maya and Daniel decide to do?
options: Delay the entire onboarding release until the recovery changes are fully tested.
Release all of the changes tomorrow and reduce the amount of testing.
Release the main onboarding changes tomorrow and move the recovery changes to the next release.
Remove the onboarding changes from the sprint and ask Sales to change its plans.
question.explanation: They keep the planned release for the main onboarding changes, but move the recovery changes to the next release so they can be tested properly.
